subject: Renewal: exploring annual prepay vs multi-year structure to mitigate price increases
messages:
From: Ben Whitaker <ben.whitaker@finex.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@finex.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — avoiding the expected rate jump

Karthik,

Thanks again for the check-in today. We're starting internal planning for our May renewal and want to avoid the sticker shock we saw in other vendors (some are quoting ~20% increases year-over-year).

Current snapshot: our usage is projecting ~2x over the next 12 months as we roll the product into two more regions. If we sign a longer commitment, we want confidence that unit economics won't drift up mid-term.

Questions:
- Do you have a clean annual prepay option (12 months) that locks today's pricing?
- Alternatively, what would a multi-year prepay look like with a stepped ramp schedule (so we don't overcommit early but lock a floor)?
- Any standard ramp-credit mechanics for volume growth in Y1? We want something that scales without penalizing faster adoption.

Can you send a short proposal we can circulate with procurement? Ideally something that shows the math (list price, discount, prepay amount, overage pricing, and true-up cadence).

Thanks — trying to get this in front of our CFO this week.

Ben
Ben Whitaker
Head of Platform, Finex Analytics
attn: procurement@finex.ai

---
Attachments: Finex_expected_usage.csv (spreadsheet, 42KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Whitaker <ben.whitaker@finex.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — avoiding the expected rate jump

Ben — appreciate the detail and urgency. High level answers inline, followed by a short proposal attached.

Short answers:
- Yes — we offer a 12-month annual prepay that can lock current unit pricing for the contract term. That is our simplest path for customers who want predictable billing and a straight price lock.
- For customers expecting fast growth we often recommend a hybrid: a shorter initial annual prepay for immediate price protection + follow-on committed prepay in years 2–3 with staged credits to accommodate ramp.
- Ramp credits: we can apply incremental credits (applied as bill-back or adjustments) for realized growth above forecast in the first 6–12 months — typical range 5–12% of the incremental spend depending on the commit profile.

Attached is a draft (Finex_MA_proposal_v1.pdf) that shows two options: A) 12-month annual prepay (price lock) and B) 3-year staggered prepay with year-by-year ramp credits and step discounts. The proposal includes a sample true-up cadence (quarterly) and overage math.

If you want, we can convert option B into an 18-month variant (front-loaded cushion + two yearly renewals) — might fit if procurement prefers fewer contract events.

I put Laura and Vivek on copy to help with approvals and commercial packaging.

Next step: tell me which option procurement prefers (A or B or hybrid) and we’ll send a redlined offer you can circulate.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Field Sales — Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — avoiding the expected rate jump

Looping finance in. A couple of practical constraints from Revenue & Finance:
- Discounting profile: we can offer up to 18% on committed multi-year deals (GAAP/recognition constraints apply). Anything above requires CFO sign-off.
- Ramp credits need to be explicit credit lines in the SOW or handled as an invoice adjustment at quarter-end; we prefer invoice adjustments for simplicity.
- PO and payment terms: for prepay we want standard 30-day net from invoice; if Finex needs 60+ day terms we should price-in an NNN adjustment.

If Karthik wants to push for a deeper early-year credit (10%+), we need a clear usage trigger and an accounting treatment (credit memo vs. deferred revenue).

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Whitaker <ben.whitaker@finex.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@finex.ai, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — avoiding the expected rate jump

Thanks Karthik & team — viewed the proposal. A few clarifications / ask from procurement: 

1) Simpler is better for legal and budget cycles. Procurement would prefer a 12-month renewable prepay that locks price for the 12 months, with a quarterly true-up and the ability to convert to a multi-year arrangement before renewal if we choose.

2) Overage cap: we want to cap any overage rate at no more than a 40% premium over our committed unit price (historically vendors quote >100% and that kills predictability).

3) Ramp credit: request a 10% credit on incremental spend above baseline in the first 9 months, applied as a quarterly invoice credit. Baseline is current average monthly usage (we attached expected numbers).

I've attached our expected usage file so you can validate the numbers against the proposal.

Ben

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — avoiding the expected rate jump

Ben — thanks for the clear asks. Below is a revised commercial that balances procurement simplicity and Finex's growth profile. This is intended to be the offer we send for signature (DocuSign link included below).

Final proposed structure (Option C — streamlined annual prepay with conversion path):
- Term: 12 months initial prepay, renewable. Refunds: none; prepay is applied to usage.
- Price protection: lock current unit price for the 12-month period. If Finex converts to a multi-year prepay before renewal, the price remains locked for the remainder of signed term.
- Overage: capped at +40% of the committed unit price as requested.
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-ups with invoice adjustments; any ramp credit applied as a credit memo at quarter-end.
- Ramp credit: 10% credit on incremental usage above baseline for the first 9 months (applies only to incremental tokens billed during that period). Credit will appear as a line item credit on the following quarter invoice.
- Conversion path: if Finex elects a multi-year prepay within the first 9 months, we will offer a stepped discount schedule (year 2 + year 3) consistent with the original Option B; conversion is applied prospectively.
- Payment: 30 days net on invoices. If procurement requires 60+ day terms, a financing uplift will apply (to be agreed).

Action items:
1) Ben/procurement to confirm baseline number (I validated your CSV against our usage; looks consistent).
2) Laura — if we agree, please provision a clean order form and route to Contracts for a short SOW (we want the true-up and credit language explicit).
3) Ben — sign via DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/Signing/?t=Finex-Prepay-Offer-v2

If that sounds good I'll have Marissa confirm the final discount line and I'll route to contracts.

Karthik
